explain.narrative:
## Generics Fundamentals and Type Parameters

Generics let classes and methods work with types while preserving compile-time checks. Parameterized collections avoid unsafe casts.

Identify the input and desired result. Select the Java construct or API that supports the requirement. Keep code readable, handle documented failures and state assumptions clearly.

Compile with JDK 21, predict output before running, and test normal, boundary and invalid inputs.

examples.title: Core API
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { java.util.List<String> names = new java.util.ArrayList<>(); names.add("Asha"); System.out.println(names.get(0)); } }
examples.explanation: A parameterized List stores String values safely.

examples.title: Practical use
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { class Box<T> { private final T value; Box(T value) { this.value=value; } T get() { return value; } } Box<Integer> box = new Box<>(7); System.out.println(box.get()); } }
examples.explanation: A generic class uses a type parameter for its stored value.

examples.title: Boundary behavior
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { java.util.List<Integer> values = java.util.List.of(1,2,3); System.out.println(values.get(2) + 1); } }
examples.explanation: A typed collection returns Integer values without manual casts.

examples.title: Alternative pattern
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { java.util.Map<String,Integer> scores = java.util.Map.of("Asha",90); System.out.println(scores.get("Asha")); } }
examples.explanation: A Map has separate key and value type parameters.

examples.title: Verify the result
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { System.out.println("Parameterized types are checked at compile time"); } }
examples.expectedOutput: Parameterized types are checked at compile time
examples.explanation: Summarizes the main safety benefit of generics.

practise.guidedTask: Create a generic Box<T> class and use it with String and Integer. Show how the compiler rejects assigning the wrong type.
practise.independentTask: Refactor a raw List into List<String>, remove unnecessary casts and demonstrate a compile-time type mismatch.
hints: Start with a small, deterministic dataset and predict the result.
Check the relevant Java interface and method contract.
Compile with JDK 21 and test duplicate, empty and boundary cases.
practise.challenge: Create a generic Pair<K,V> class and use it for a product code and price; explain why primitive types need wrapper classes.
